title: Unhindered (Acts 28:17–31)
hookLine: Acts ends with Paul in Rome under guard, welcoming all, preaching without hindrance
tomorrow: a church splits into fan clubs. whose club does Paul go after first?

lines: A GUARD, A CHAIN, A ROOM.
cards: Some endings feel unfinished: a show canceled mid-season, a friend who moves before you said the thing. Acts ends a little like that. Paul reaches Rome at last, and he isn't in a cell.
He "was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him." A place of his own, a guard at the door, and a chain. Visitors can come in.
He can't go out. Then a few scenes, and the book stops.

teach.b: He calls together the leaders of the Jewish community in Rome and tells them why he's bound: "for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain." They've heard nothing against him, they say, and they want to hear him out.
So they come to his lodging, and from morning till evening he talks.
Acts reports the result plainly: "And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not."

Then the last verses of the book: "And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him, Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him."
No trial scene. No verdict from Caesar. Acts doesn't say what happened next.

teach.h: THE BOOK STOPS IN AN OPEN ROOM.
teach.b: It stops in an open room: the chain still on, the guard still there, and everyone who comes let in. For a week when you can't change much, that's what this ending hands you.
Not freedom from the chain. A door you choose to keep open.

how: Some churches read from Acts in the weeks after Easter, and readers who go straight through notice that the book ends without telling how Paul's trial turned out.

games.q: you're stuck at home all summer with a cast on your leg. what does the end of Acts suggest?
o: wait it out; nothing good happens until the cast is off.
keep the door open: let people come, and give what you have.
push yourself out anyway, so you don't miss anything.
games.why: Paul stayed chained in one house for two whole years and received all that came in. the room was small; the door was open.

practice: Pick up your phone and find one name you haven't heard from in a while, someone you'd be glad to see at your door. Send one plain line that leaves the door open, with nothing asked back. Then set the phone face down and rest.

wordCard.voice: Unhindered. How Acts ends: a prisoner in a hired house, a chain on his wrist, welcoming all, and no one stopping him.

orig.note: Greek: unhindered, without hindrance. The King James gives it as no man forbidding him.

carryVoice: Keep this one: no man forbidding him, chain still on and door still open. That's the book of Acts.
